London, 23<sup>rd</sup> March 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**A gain in Europe’s largest new-vehicle market** couldn’t overcome continued massive losses elsewhere last month.  European new-vehicle sales plunged 18.3 % in February to 968,159 units.  Aided by new government subsidies for scrapping older cars, German new-car sales jumped 21.5 % in February to 277,740. Besides Germany, only Poland and Luxembourg increased sales. Italy, France, the UK and Spain — the rest of Europe’s five largest markets — posted double-digit losses.  Among brands, the only sales increases in February came from Suzuki and Smart, both up 0.6 %; Alfa Romeo, up 23.3%; Hyundai, up 20.2 %; and Jaguar, up 12.3 %.  From No. 6 in 2008, Italy’s Fiat Group moved to No. 4 among European automakers, leapfrogging General Motors and Renault SA. Fiat sales fell 21.2% in the first two months to 171,239, almost as bad as the industry’s 22.6 % decline. But GM’s fell 29.1% to 166,722, and Renault dropped 28.5 % to 156,425.  Two other mass-market auto groups gained market share in February despite declining volume, because they weren’t as bad as the rest of the industry. Volkswagen AG fell 10.2 % to 210,337 units but increased its European market share to 21.7 % from 19.8 % a year earlier. Ford sales dropped 12.7 % to 95,164 units, but its market share rose 0.6 points to 9.8%.  Daimler AG was the biggest loser among Europe’s 10 largest automakers, down 29.8% overall. BMW Group fell almost as much, by 29.2 % to 40,928 on weak results for both the BMW and Mini brands. 

## _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Daimler Trucks** chief Andreas Renschler said that the global commercial vehicles market will see another sharp decline this year.  Renschler said he expected the European market to decline between 30 - 50 %, although “the tendency is more towards 50 %”.  The NAFTA region is expected to shrink 30 % and Japan 40 %.  According to data from the ACEA, the European heavy truck market contracted by 2 % to about 314,000 vehicles last year, mainly on a sharp drop in demand among new EU member states.  Daimler will cut jobs and investments at its truck division - the world’s largest manufacturer of commercial vehicles - and aims for savings of more than 1 billion euros ($1.37 billion) in two years.  However, Daimler will still continue to drive expansion in growth markets such as China, India and Russia, he said.  After declining by 76 % in January, new orders from abroad for German-made trucks weighing 6 tonnes and more collapsed 95 % in February, according to the German automotive industry association VDA.  J.P. Morgan forecast European truck volumes would halve this year in the worst downturn for the sector since World War Two. 

## _Source:  The Guardian_ 

**Nissan** expects to boost domestic vehicle sales next fiscal year, as tax breaks spur demand for compact cars and other fuel-efficient models.  The carmaker is tentatively targeting a 10 % rise to 660,000 vehicles in the yea

r starting April 1, the Nikkan Jidosha reported.  Japan will offer tax breaks on fuelefficient cars from April 1 in a bid to revive demand. Domestic auto sales, excluding minicars, fell for a seventh straight month in February, dropping 32 %, because of the recession.  Nissan will set a formal sales target in April, taking into account industrywide demand, the newspaper said. 

## _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Zurich Cantonal Bank** (ZKB) said last Wednesday that its platinum ETF ZPLA.S holdings have risen 22 % since February to 160,800 ounces, while holdings of its silver-backed product ZSIL.S have climbed 4.38 million ounces or 11.5 % to 42.889 million ounces.  The bank said holdings of its palladium-backed ETF ZPAL.S had also ticked up 2 % or 12,600 ounces to 544,600 ounces.
